app.title: ViewAlign (MSA-viewer)
app.summary: A person loads a multiple sequence alignment by dropping or pasting a file in one of several formats. They look across it with conservation shading and a consensus row, switching between continuous, wrapped-block and canvas layouts and narrowing to the variable columns. They fix it by hand: they type residues, slide stretches, insert or delete gaps, realign a selected block with an in-browser aligner, and trim gappy ends, with undo throughout. They can then group sequences into subfamilies, search for motifs, build a tree or statistics, and leave with a corrected alignment as FASTA, a consensus, a Newick tree, or an SVG or RTF figure for publication.

task.text: Inspect, hand-correct and annotate a multiple sequence alignment, then export it, its consensus or a figure for publication.

data.text: A set of aligned DNA or protein sequences, one row per sequence and one column per aligned position. Optional extras are BED feature annotations, sequencing chromatograms and mapped reads against a reference.
data.item: an aligned sequence (a row), and one column of residues across all the rows

stage.text: checking and hand-correcting alignments after automatic alignment, before tree building or publication figures

mechanism.text: A large scrolling grid of residues is shaded by per-column conservation under a consensus row. Menus above it change thresholds, layout and colouring, and apply edits, realignment, trimming, clustering and searches that redraw the grid. Separate windows draw a tree and statistics from the current alignment or selection.

field.text: multiple sequence alignment editing and analysis in molecular biology

workflow.name: inspect and hand-correct an alignment of many ordered strings, then export it

steps.here: drop or paste FASTA, MSF, Clustal, PHYLIP, NEXUS, Stockholm, GenBank or AB1 text into the Input box and press Load; recent files, saved snapshots and server paths are offered too

steps.step: look over every item at a glance
steps.here: the alignment is drawn as a residue grid shaded black, dark or light by column conservation under a consensus row; Full, Block and Canvas modes, zoom, and 'Variable sites only' change what is shown

steps.step: find and fix problems by hand
steps.here: Edit mode gives Move NoGaps, Slide KeepGaps, gap insert and delete per sequence, per other sequences or per column, and residue typing; Degap removes gap-only columns, with undo and redo history

steps.step: compute a value from the data
steps.here: selected rows or a column block are realigned with in-browser MAFFT or codon-aware MACSE and spliced back in; gappy ends are previewed and trimmed by gap percentage
sequences are grouped by k-mer tree or by shared position patterns, and their names and distinctive bases are coloured

steps.step: filter to the items that matter
steps.here: motif or regex search with mismatches and both strands, and restriction sites, highlight hits in chosen colours
Copy or Save the alignment as FASTA, copy the consensus, save a Newick tree, export a viewport or full SVG or a shaded RTF, or save a snapshot

distinctive: Conservation shading uses three adjustable identity thresholds, and gaps can count against conservation or be ignored
A consensus row with a threshold, a minimum coverage and an IUPAC ambiguity option can be inserted below any selected group
Codon analysis translates in a chosen frame and genetic code, and flags stop codons, frameshifts and synonymous vs non-synonymous changes
A region can be realigned in place with an aligner that runs in the browser, while the rest of the alignment stays as it is
Alignments with millions of residues are drawn by windowed and canvas renderers, so scrolling stays usable

parts.title: Input and export menu
parts.summary: Loads an alignment from a dropped file, pasted text, recent history or a snapshot, and saves it back out as FASTA, SVG, RTF or a snapshot.

spans.first: <button id="copyAlignToolbarButton" class="edit-toggle-button" title="Copy entire alignment to clipboard (FASTA)" onclic

parts.title: Alignment grid
parts.summary: Shows every sequence as a row of residues, with sticky names, zoom, block wrapping, canvas mode for large alignments and a variable-sites-only filter.

spans.first: Paste MSF or FASTA into the box and click Load, or drop a file.

parts.title: Shade and consensus controls
parts.summary: Sets the three conservation thresholds and colours, and the consensus threshold, coverage, ambiguity type and position, with copy and insert-below actions.

parts.title: Edit toolbar and history
parts.summary: Provides GeneDoc-style tools to move residues, slide stretches, insert or delete gaps and type residues, with undo and redo history.

spans.first: <button id="editToggleButton" class="edit-toggle-button" aria-pressed="false" title="Toggle GeneDoc-style sequence editi

parts.title: Alignment menu
parts.summary: Realigns all sequences, the selected sequences or a selected block with in-browser MAFFT or codon-aware MACSE, adds new sequences, and reorders rows by similarity.

parts.title: Trimming and clustering panel
parts.summary: Trims gappy alignment ends from a preview, and groups sequences into subfamilies by k-mer tree or position patterns, colouring their names and distinctive bases.

parts.title: Motif search
parts.summary: Finds motifs, regular expressions or restriction sites in the ungapped sequences, allowing mismatches and both strands, and highlights each search in its own colour.

parts.title: Tree and statistics windows
parts.summary: Builds a UPGMA or neighbour-joining tree under a chosen distance model and exports it as Newick, and shows a pairwise identity and distance matrix with summary statistics.
